title: Serialize repeating volume adjustments

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A lock-file open error becomes a successful, silent volume no-op
leads.consequence: With an invalid, missing or unwritable XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, exec {lock_fd}> fails, leaving lock_fd empty; flock -n receives an invalid descriptor and `|| exit 0` skips sink lookup and every pactl/OSD action. Even with a valid runtime directory, an inherited `SHELLOPTS=noclobber` makes the first invocation work but every later invocation fail against its existing lock file while still returning success. Flock errors such as resource failures are also treated as intentional contention. Require a successful open and distinguish genuine contention from errors (or return nonzero on inability to lock).
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1); corroboration noted; noclobber variant not published

leads.summary: The /tmp fallback uses one shared, predictable lock-file name
leads.consequence: If XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset/empty, every account tries to open the identical /tmp/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock with `>`. An unwritable pre-existing file blocks the volume command persistently (and I-1 makes it return 0); a writable symlink in the selected runtime directory is followed and the target truncated before flock runs. The desktop's normal private XDG runtime directory avoids cross-user collision, but a CLI run from an environment without it does not. Choose a private per-user directory/fd and do not truncate or follow untrusted lock paths.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up 1 Q2; with default fs protections only a lock-open failure (same as N1); established pattern in other scripts

leads.summary: With open #8096, adjusting one named sink drops an unrelated sink's adjustment
leads.consequence: #8096 forwards an optional sink name as argv[2] to the resolver, but this PR locks one fixed path before looking at argv[2]. After both merge, a busy sink1 volume command causes a single `+1 sink2` to return success before it even resolves sink2, whereas #8096 alone adjusts sink2. This is not merely a textual conflict: the three-way merge succeeds, both PRs are diverged and GitHub lists #8096 as MERGEABLE. Serialize per resolved sink (or preserve non-repeat named actions) and test two simultaneous distinct sink names.
leads.triage: behavioural; confirmed by Opus follow-up 1 run 4; published with realism qualifier

leads.summary: A clean merge of open #7273 makes this PR's new test fail
leads.consequence: The fixture always reads 50%, then asserts `osd -i volume-high -p 50`. #7273 intentionally introduces low/medium/high icons with 50% mapped to `volume-medium`. Both changes merge without markers, and #7273's own icon test passes, but this PR's test exits 1 at the OSD assertion. Update this expectation (or choose a percentage unaffected by the icon bands) if #7273 merges; otherwise CI fails for a correct combined implementation.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (L1); corroboration noted

leads.summary: The concurrency test can pass when most repeatable actions remain unlocked
leads.consequence: All three cases invoke only `raise` and `mute-toggle`, while the new guard also promises `lower`, `+N` and `-N`. A plausible regression, changing the guard to lock only `raise`, passes every assertion; those other stock repeatable actions (notably Alt+Volume +/-1, current tip media.lua:18-19) again spawn overlapping pactl clients. Add lock-held negative-call assertions for lower, +1 and -1, plus successful unlocked controls for each.
leads.triage: confirmed by Opus follow-up 1 mutants run 4; published

limits: No real Hyprland key-repeat hardware or host audio was used. Controlled mocks inside review.py establish the documented call and test outcomes, not on-device timing or pipewire-pulse exhaustion.

The cross-user /tmp collision in I-2 was tested with a pre-existing unwritable stand-in file, not by creating another OS identity. Filesystem protections on a particular host can restrict symlink-following in sticky directories; the symlink truncation run used a private stand-in runtime directory.
Additional open PRs in broad topic searches whose diffs do not change the volume script or its named resolver were triaged as non-overlapping; no claim that this is a census of all future PRs.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new test fails once open PR #7273 lands.

### New test pins the OSD icon that #7273 changes

The test asserts `osd -i volume-high -p 50`, but #7273 shows `volume-medium` for 34-66%. With both merged on current `quattro`, the test fails.

**Suggested change:** match the OSD call without the icon, for example `grep -Eq '^osd -i [a-z-]+ -p 50$'`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails on quattro + this PR + #7273)</summary>

# Reproducer: the new test pins the OSD icon, which #7273 changes

The first case of `test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-concurrency-test.sh` asserts the exact OSD line `osd -i volume-high -p 50`. Open PR #7273 ("Match the volume OSD icon to the output switcher") makes `omarchy-audio-output-volume` show `volume-medium` for 34-66%, so the stubbed 50% no longer maps to `volume-high`.

Tree: `quattro` at 8b4eae66 with this PR applied, then #7273's head (c6dda1a) merged on top. Both merge without conflicts.

```bash
bash test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-concurrency-test.sh
```

Actual result: stdout empty, exit status 1, stderr:

```text
not ok - volume raise shows the OSD
```

## Icon-agnostic assertion

Changing only the OSD assertion in the PR's test:

```diff
-grep -Fx 'osd -i volume-high -p 50' "$call_log" >/dev/null || fail "volume raise shows the OSD"
+grep -Eq '^osd -i [a-z-]+ -p 50$' "$call_log" || fail "volume raise shows the OSD"
```

Actual result on the same merged tree: exit status 0, stderr empty, stdout:

```text
ok - volume raise updates the sink and shows the OSD
ok - overlapping volume events exit before opening audio clients
ok - mute remains responsive during a volume adjustment
```

The same edited test also passes at the PR head (bb1f2c1): exit status 0, the same three `ok` lines.

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- Overlapping `raise`/`lower`/`+N`/`-N` runs exit 0 before any `pactl` call; accepted runs are serialized and `mute-toggle` stays unlocked.
- In a stub burst (80 launches 25 ms apart, stub `pactl` taking 20 ms per call), peak concurrent `pactl` clients fell from 6 to 1, and volume steps lost fell from 40 to 0.
- The new test fails its overlap case against the current `quattro` script.

**Scope on current `quattro`:** since #13424, plain volume keys on an ALSA default sink are handled in the shell and do not run this script. The lock still applies to `ALT` + volume (`+1`/`-1`) and to plain keys on non-ALSA sinks (Bluetooth, DSP chains).

**Optional robustness guard:** if `exec {lock_fd}>` fails (for example a non-writable `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`), `flock -n ""` fails and `|| exit 0` exits 0 without changing the volume; before this PR the call applied. Reach is low, since a graphical session has a writable runtime directory. Exiting only when the lock is actually held avoids it: `if exec {lock_fd}>"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock" && ! flock -n "$lock_fd"; then exit 0; fi`. Reproducer in the next block.

**Optional test improvement:** the overlap case only sends `raise`, so a mutant that locks only `raise` passes the whole test. Sending `lower`, `+1` and `-1` while the lock is held catches it. Reproducer in the last block.

**Related open PR:** with #8096 (optional sink argument), the single per-user lock would also drop, silently and with exit 0, a concurrent step aimed at a different sink. No caller in the repository passes a sink name, so only user-made bindings or commands would be affected.
</details>

<details><summary>Lock-failure reproducer (fails at bb1f2c1)</summary>

Local paths in this output are replaced with placeholders (`<pr-head-copy>`, `<fixed-copy>`, `<test_dir>`); the rest is unchanged.

# Reproducer: an unopenable lock file silently drops every adjustment

When `exec {lock_fd}>".../omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock"` fails (for example `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is not writable, or it is unset and `/tmp/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock` belongs to another user), `lock_fd` stays empty, `flock -n ""` fails, and `|| exit 0` exits successfully without changing the volume. Before this PR the same call adjusted the volume.

Case appended to the end of `test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-concurrency-test.sh` at the PR head (bb1f2c1):

```bash
# The lock file cannot be created: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not writable.
ro_runtime="$test_dir/ro-runtime"
mkdir -p "$ro_runtime"
chmod 555 "$ro_runtime"
: >"$call_log"
PATH="$test_dir/bin:$PATH" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$ro_runtime" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-audio-output-volume" raise || true

grep -Fx 'pactl set-sink-volume test_sink 55%' "$call_log" >/dev/null || fail "volume raise still applies when the lock file cannot be created"
pass "volume raise still applies when the lock file cannot be created"
```

Run as a non-root user (uid 1000) from a copy of the PR head at `<pr-head-copy>`:

```bash
bash test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-concurrency-test.sh
```

Actual result: exit status 1. stdout:

```text
ok - volume raise updates the sink and shows the OSD
ok - overlapping volume events exit before opening audio clients
ok - mute remains responsive during a volume adjustment
```

stderr:

```text
<pr-head-copy>/bin/omarchy-audio-output-volume: line 18: <test_dir>/ro-runtime/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock: Permission denied
flock: bad file descriptor: ''
not ok - volume raise still applies when the lock file cannot be created
```

## Guard that only drops when the lock is actually held

```diff
 if [[ $action == "raise" || $action == "lower" || $action =~ ^[+-][0-9]+$ ]]; then
-  exec {lock_fd}>"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock"
-  flock -n "$lock_fd" || exit 0
+  if exec {lock_fd}>"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock" && ! flock -n "$lock_fd"; then
+    exit 0
+  fi
 fi
```

Actual result of the same test file with this guard applied (copy at `<fixed-copy>`): exit status 0. stdout:

```text
ok - volume raise updates the sink and shows the OSD
ok - overlapping volume events exit before opening audio clients
ok - mute remains responsive during a volume adjustment
ok - volume raise still applies when the lock file cannot be created
```

stderr:

```text
<fixed-copy>/bin/omarchy-audio-output-volume: line 18: <test_dir>/ro-runtime/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock: Permission denied
```

Reach: a graphical Omarchy session always has a writable `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, and `bin/omarchy-brightness-display` (lines 76-77) uses the same `|| exit 0` pattern, so this only matters outside a normal session.

</details>

<details><summary>Mutant reproducer</summary>

# Reproducer: the PR test does not pin which actions are locked

Each mutant changes only the lock condition on line 17 of `bin/omarchy-audio-output-volume` at the PR head (bb1f2c1). For example, the raise-only mutant:

```diff
@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@
 # Drop overlapping volume adjustments so hardware key repeat does not flood
 # pipewire-pulse with short-lived pactl clients. Leave mute independent so a
 # press is not lost behind an adjustment already in flight.
-if [[ $action == "raise" || $action == "lower" || $action =~ ^[+-][0-9]+$ ]]; then
+if [[ $action == "raise" ]]; then
   exec {lock_fd}>"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-audio-output-volume.lock"
   flock -n "$lock_fd" || exit 0
 fi
```

The other mutant conditions:

- no-signed-steps: `if [[ $action == "raise" || $action == "lower" ]]; then`
- no-lower: `if [[ $action == "raise" || $action =~ ^[+-][0-9]+$ ]]; then`
- no-lock (control): `if false; then`
- lock-mute-too (control): `if true; then`

Command, run from each mutated copy: `bash test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-concurrency-test.sh`
